chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If you fear that you will not be able to stand [for prayer] at the end of the night, or if you have an ailment, or if cold affects you, then perform your prayer and offer the Witr prayer from the beginning of the night."
ai.seo_question: When can I pray Witr if I fear I won't wake up for Tahajjud?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the permissibility of advancing the Witr prayer when there is a genuine fear of missing it due to sleep or physical weakness. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *rukhsah* (concession), prioritizing the consistency of performing the prayer over the strict adherence to its preferred late-night timing, thereby ensuring the worshipper does not abandon the Sunnah entirely.
